input.quote: (b) Licensee agrees to allow an independent Certified Public Accountant or other Audit Professional, (selected by mutual agreement) to audit and analyze appropriate accounting records to ensure compliance with all terms of this Agreement. Any such audit shall be permitted by Licensee within 30 days of Licensee's receipt of a written request of Licensor.
input.rationale: Article II.IV(b) binds Licensee to permit Licensor-requested audits with no cap on frequency, no minimum notice period (the 30 days is a deadline to submit, not advance notice), no business-hours or off-site limitation, no restriction on system access and no confidentiality undertaking from the auditor. Unlimited audits approach our walk-away position. The auditor is at least independent and mutually selected, and cost allocation in p0064 (Licensor bears cost unless a 5% discrepancy) already matches our preferred position, so the minimal fix is to add frequency, notice, business-hours, off-site/no-system-access and auditor confidentiality limits to p0073.

ops.oldText: Any such audit shall be permitted by Licensee within 30 days of Licensee's receipt of a written request of Licensor.
ops.newText: Any such audit shall occur no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, shall be conducted during Licensee's normal business hours on not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice from Licensor, shall be conducted off-site wherever practicable, and shall not include any direct or remote access to Licensee's systems, networks or premises. The auditor shall first execute written confidentiality undertakings in favor of Licensee no less protective than those set forth in this Agreement.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We limited the audit right to once per twelve months on thirty days' written notice, during business hours, off-site where practicable and with no access to our systems, and required the auditor to be bound by confidentiality. Cost allocation already sits with Licensor unless a 5% discrepancy is found, which works for us; if needed we can live with fifteen days' notice.
proposal.summary: Cap audit frequency and add notice, business-hours, confidentiality and no-system-access limits.
